The reaction sequence involves bromination of cyclohexanone to give 2-bromocyclohexanone (1), which undergoes Favorskii rearrangement with hot NaOH to form cyclopentanecarboxylic acid (2). This acid is converted to its acid chloride with SOCl₂/pyridine (3), and reduction with lithium tri-tert-butoxyaluminum hydride yields cyclopentanecarboxaldehyde (4). The molecule has an aldehyde hydrogen, a methine hydrogen on the ring carbon bearing the aldehyde, and two sets of equivalent methylene hydrogens (adjacent and opposite to the substituent) due to symmetry, giving a total of four chemically distinct hydrogen atoms.

ANSWER: 4
